In [[cryptography]], '''NUSH''' is a [[block cipher]] invented by [[Anatoly Lebedev]] and [[Alexey Volchkov]] for the Russian company [[LAN Crypto]]. It was submitted to the [[NESSIE]] project, but was not selected.

NUSH exists in several different variants, using keys of 128, 192, or 256 bits, and a block size of 64, 128, or 256 bits. The number of rounds is 9, 17, or 33, depending on the block size. The algorithm uses [[key whitening]], but no [[substitution box|S-boxes]]; the only operations it uses are [[Binary and|AND]], [[Logical disjunction|OR]], [[XOR]], [[modular arithmetic|modular addition]], and [[bit rotation]].

It has been shown that [[linear cryptanalysis]] can break NUSH with less effort than a [[brute force attack]].<ref>{{cite journal
| title=Linear cryptanalysis of NUSH block cipher
| author=Wenling Wu, Dengguo Feng
| date=23 July 2001
| journal=Science China Information Sciences

}}</ref>
